_comment: Authored desired-truth registry for scripts/check-invariants.sh. It is distinct from collected inventory and generated docs. Each entry carries the current rationale required to operate the constraint. Changing ops_managed_pools moves the blast-radius dial and requires a docs/system-design.md PR (§2b). Doctrine: docs/decisions/0003-ambiguity-layering-and-format-follows-enforcement.md.

excluded_guests.why: These guests are permanently unpooled. Pool membership is the enforced line: joining any to an ops-managed pool hands the agent full T2 write, so the gate fails any PR where one appears as a member. Envelope reach depends on the node (see operate_token_scope): on NETWORK the token remains pool-scoped, so opnsense 5001, caddy-mgmt 635, and authentik 837 are unreachable and never stopped/reconfigured by the agent. On CORE the root-/ operate ACL makes Unraid 2020 envelope-reachable for config/power, but policy keeps it unpooled and never-destroyed while guest-OS root stays T3 (t3_targets). See docs/system-design.md §2b/§3 and docs/design/access-and-trust.md.

guests.name: vm-opnsense
guests.why: the firewall/router itself; DHCP + all inter-VLAN routing depend on it. Never poolable.

guests.name: lxc-caddy-management
guests.why: the Management Caddy (the privileged front door). T3 by constitution §3.

guests.name: lxc-authentik
guests.why: Authentik server administration is T3 (app/provider provisioning is a separate scoped T2 token, not pool membership).

guests.name: vm-unraid
guests.why: Unraid storage host; root over it is T3. Never poolable.

construction.why: The unprivileged NixOS aliammar account is the filesystem/OS construction boundary. Home Manager sets Codex approval_policy=never and sandbox_mode=danger-full-access so Main and native workers can perform ordinary account-accessible work without prompts; no project or role sandbox may override that inherited session posture. This grants no production authority: credentials, trust tiers, human merge, and hard forbidden rules for gh pr merge and both grant-root spellings remain separate boundaries. Concurrency and worker ownership remain governed by the construction doctrine.

agents.why: persistent read-only project-context secretary by ownership and instructions
disposable read-only evidence researcher by ownership and instructions
owns bounded implementation and ordinary repair
owns one exceptionally hard bounded implementation package
owns independent verification, never production repair
owns assigned stable memory and documentation, never acceptance

entity_conventions.why: The VMID/IP law (ADR 0001 and docs/conventions/naming.md) derives a guest address from its VLAN and last two VMID digits. The invariant gate requires every running entity to be mapped or declared here. T3 guests are listed separately in excluded_guests; this list is for intentionally unmapped running guests. Changing declared_vlans requires a docs/conventions/naming.md change.

ops_managed_pools.why: THE blast-radius dial. Write blast radius = this pool set (+ ROLE_OPS_SSH_TARGETS + Technitium zones). The gate asserts the ops-managed pools observed in inventory match this declared set — drift either way is a violation (an undeclared pool is as dangerous as a missing one). Changing this set is a docs/system-design.md PR (constitution §2b); it is NOT collected/generated.

pools.why: the ops-managed pool on the core node; current position of the dial.
the ops-managed pool on the network node; current position of the dial.

operate_token_scope.why: The operate token may allocate VM envelopes at /vms on the declared core node, so pool membership alone does not describe its reach. The gate reads each node's collected ACL and rejects forbidden privileges everywhere; node-root VM allocation may appear only on vms_root_nodes. Widening either boundary requires a docs/system-design.md PR. Excluded guests remain unpooled, and the network node has no /vms allocation because it hosts OPNsense and enforces the agent's leash.

vms_root_nodes.why: Allocates managed pool guests. The network node remains pool-membership-scoped.

t3_targets.why: The never-standing-credential list (constitution §2a / §3, AGENTS.md §6). No standing route or credential that can CHANGE any of these — reached only via a dormant alias + per-session credentials, revoked same day. OPNsense is the tiered exception (ADR 0006): read+diagnostics T1, firewall CONFIG T2 (PR-gated via OpenTofu), but the entries below stay never-standing. Documented here now as desired truth; future checks (e.g. asserting no standing WRITE token references these) build on it.

targets.name: OPNsense node root / account / cert / reboot
targets.why: OPNsense is tiered (ADR 0006): read+diagnostics T1, firewall config T2 (aliases/rules via OpenTofu, PR-gated). But node root, API-key/cert admin, and REBOOT/halt (a lab-wide outage — hard checkpoint at every tier) stay T3, never-standing. See ADR 0006 / docs/design/access-and-trust.md.

targets.name: OPNsense self-leash rules
targets.why: The agent never changes rules or aliases bounding its own reach: ROLE_OPS_*, ROLE_OPS_PRIV_TARGETS, block-other-DNS, and its OPNsense accounts. This boundary remains human-merged and T3 even when other firewall config is T2.

targets.name: Authentik server admin
targets.why: flows, policies, users, system settings, outpost tokens, signing keys stay T3 (VMID 837).

targets.name: Proxmox node root
targets.why: root on either hypervisor node is T3.

targets.name: Unraid root
targets.why: root on the storage host (VMID 2020) is T3.

targets.name: Technitium server settings
targets.why: Settings/Administration/DHCP are T3; only Zones view/modify is T2.

secret_patterns.why: Plaintext-secret signatures the gate greps for in tracked, non-encrypted files. Hard law: secrets are sops-encrypted in git (compose/*/.env.sops) or 0600 under /opt/skynet-ops/secrets/ — never plaintext in commits, logs, transcripts, or chat (constitution §2a). A hit fails the PR.

allow.why: sops-encrypted payloads are ciphertext by definition — the intended home for secrets in git.
holds only the age PUBLIC recipient key (age1...), which is not secret.
this file lists the patterns themselves as data; it contains no live secret.

patterns.why: an age PRIVATE key (prefix + bech32 body); the master secret of the whole vault. Must only ever exist at /opt/skynet-ops/secrets/age.key + the survival kit. Requiring the key body means prose that merely mentions the prefix does not trip.
any PEM private key block (OpenSSH/RSA/EC/PKCS8) — SSH or TLS private material must never be committed in plaintext.
a Proxmox API token secret (user@realm!tokenid=UUID) — a live write/read credential to the cluster.
